newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark eyes break from tight range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark eyes break from tight range.

text.p: Dollar/mark's range between 1.7850 and 1.8050 is sure to be history by week's end, the upshot being levels beyond six-year highs, technical analysts said on Monday.
But dollar/mark's consolidation from a 71-month high of 1.8040 may have one or two more days to go, they said, before a move higher -- or lower -- comes to fruition.
Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America, said the dollar's move should be on the upside toward 1.8240 marks.

"By the end of the week the dollar should break higher and go above 1.82," said Johnson, noting that weekly charts show a break from triangle, or sideways formation. "Then above (1.8240) you have 1991's highs between 1.84 and 1.85."
If the dollar does not break higher by week's end, Johnson said a selloff becomes more likely. The outlook would remain bullish to key supports near 1.77, he said.
Thom Worden, vice president of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's global technical analysis group, noted dollar/Swiss franc may be a key indicator of the next dollar/mark move -- be it higher or lower.

A dollar/Swiss move below 1.4705, corresponding to about 1.7880 in dollar/mark, would be a clear bearish signal for dollar/mark, Worden said. Conversely, the 1.4795 level should be watched for a break to the topside, he said.
"If we come down to 1.7880 (dollar/mark), that could mean we have had a failure to the topside," he said. "Then the risk would turn to the downside for a day or so, possibly to 1.7780 or more."
In dollar/yen, Worden said upside targets of 116.80 and 117.00 are still in place, so long as 115.40 support holds.
And Johnson noted that a move above key resistance at 117 yen could accelerate the run higher.

"Dollar/yen I think could surprise the upside," Johnson said. "You've had some pretty good resistance at 116.40, and that's been tested, but the real level to get above is 117 and the dollar could go to 120 plus."
The downside has good support at 115.20, 115.00 and then at 114.50, Johnson said, adding that the dollar could stay in its range longer than dollar/mark.
Dollar/yen may get pressured in the near-term by a downward mark/yen correction to 64.20 or 64.00, Johnson said.
